newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China warned over restricting U.S. grain imports.
newsitem.headline: China warned over restricting U.S. grain imports.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman warned China on Saturday it cannot join the World Trade Organisation if it does not adopt internationally accepted rules on resolving trade disputes.

"China can't come into the WTO, be a part of nations economically and still call it its own way when it comes to agricultural import-export practices," Glickman told Reuters in an interview on Saturday.
Glickman, in Manila to attend the annual summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, was referring to problems with China over U.S. grains exports.
China has rejected consignments of U.S. wheat in recent months saying they were disease-infected but commodities experts say the cargo may have been rejected because China had a good harvest.
"We are working with the Chinese on this and I am a little more optimistic than I might have been, let's say, a year ago," Glickman said.

"China wants to come into the WTO and wants to participate as an equal partner in world trade. But China is gonna have to play it by internationallly accepted rules, in terms of sanitary and phytosanitary standards, the way we resolve disputes, the way every other nation in the world deals with these kind of problems," he added.
The United States has opposed China's entry into the WTO, the new world trade forum which holds its first ministerial conference in Singapore next month.
Glickman said he was optimistic Sino-U.S. trade problems could be resolved, saying: "I think China has begun to recognise that it can't have it both ways."
Chinese President Jiang Zemin and U.S. President Bill Clinton are among the leaders due to attend the summit on Monday in Subic Bay, 80 kms (50 miles) north of Manila.

APEC comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
